$comment: Curated editorial metadata for the website's decision registry (website/lib/decisions.ts).
The registry is GENERATED. Identity — id, type, slug, title, path, canonical URL, status — is read
from the record itself and is never written here: the tree decides what exists and what it is
called. What cannot be read from a record is its EDITORIAL framing, and that is what this file
holds: the one-line summary shown on a card, and the theme a record is filed under.
This file exists because the registry used to claim it was generated while three records carried
hand-written summaries and categories the generator could not reproduce. Running the generator
would silently have replaced them. Ownership is now explicit: whatever is here is curated, and
everything else is derived. A record needs an entry ONLY when the derived value is wrong for it.
The derived summary is the record's first substantive paragraph, which describes the CONTEXT — the
problem that prompted the decision. For most records that reads well. For a few it buries the
decision itself, and those are the ones curated below.
category_order is the canonical order of the theme filter. A category that appears on a record but
not in this list is a generation ERROR, not a silent append: which themes exist is an editorial
decision, and the generator must not make it.

ADR-040.summary: BANZA has exactly four fundamental principles — Robust, Resilient, Secure and Simple. Resilience was the question nothing forced anyone to answer, and naming it is what makes it checkable.
ADR-040.why_curated: The record opens on the absence of a named criterion; the decision is the four principles themselves.

ADR-041.summary: No layer may validate itself. Every critical property must be demonstrated through a falsifiable chain of evidence, and a higher gate never compensates for a lower one.
ADR-041.why_curated: The record opens on an observation about accumulated green; the decision is the rule that no layer validates itself.
